video_title: Is The AI Selloff A Buying Opportunity? | Warren Pies
gist: Warren Pies (314 Research) explains why he downgraded equities to neutral despite still-bullish AI fundamentals: a near-high consolidation, financials-vs-staples breakdown and hyperscaler credit spreads above July wides, with no sentiment capitulation yet. He argues GPU data (zero B200 availability, rising rents, contango as a capacity premium), Anthropic's S1 unit economics and satellite data-center pacing show no overbuild, so the joint semis/hyperscaler selloff looks like a VaR shock, while the real risk is a Fed now focused on the AI build-out; on oil he recommends an energy overweight amid a ~45-day Iran resolution window.

insights.claim: Pies' core discipline is to build conviction on fundamentals but manage risk with technicals, and he says the technicals now override his still-bullish AI fundamentals.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: A bullish fundamental view does not preclude cutting equity exposure when price action deteriorates.
insights.quote: I build conviction on fundamentals but manage risk with technicals.

insights.claim: After running an overweight equity tilt since late 2023 (following Waller's easing signal), 314 Research downgraded stocks to neutral at the start of last week.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: A long-time bull taking risk off is a notable sentiment shift.

insights.claim: The market has entered a 'consolidation': a tight roughly 6-7% trading range over about 63 days near highs with no new highs or lows, which occurs about 13% of the time and signals lost momentum and a pending breakout or breakdown.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Consolidations near highs warrant reduced risk until the range resolves.
insights.quote: it happens at all close to all time highs or 52 week highs um and it occurs about 13%of the time.

insights.claim: The financials-versus-staples ratio is rolling over, the same leadership signal that preceded the Liberation Day sell-off and an earlier breakdown this year, with staples up about 14% in October.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Defensive leadership by staples and energy argues against a broad bull advance.
insights.quote: a market led by energy and staples is a really unhealthy market.

insights.claim: Hyperscaler credit spreads have broken above the wides from the July 'Leopold liquidation lows' before equities corrected back there, which Pies reads as shifting the default assumption from sustained uptrend to breakdown.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Watch hyperscaler credit as the lead indicator for AI equity risk.

insights.claim: Pies will only re-add risk on either a breakout from the range or a true sentiment washout; levered-plus-inverse ETF volume, internal sentiment models and vol-target positioning (still about one standard deviation above its rolling mean) have not reached capitulation.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: No capitulation yet implies further downside room before a high-odds entry.
insights.quote: You're either going to buy a breakout that's how we're positioned now or you're going to buy extreme fear, and we don't have either of those right now.

insights.claim: Pies' political contacts are concerned about a 'blue tsunami' in the midterms, and he sees pressure such as the Texas legislature slowing data center build-outs as a real risk.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Political backlash against data centers is a supply-side risk for the AI capex trade.
insights.quote: they're concerned over a blue, not just a blue wave, but a blue tsunami.

insights.claim: Year to date, the gap between S&P returns on semiconductor up-days versus down-days exceeds 105%, the widest of the roughly 50 industry groups tracked, with semis now about 20% of S&P 500 market cap.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Index direction is essentially a semis call; SMH breakdown matters for everything.

insights.claim: Pod shops and multi-strats expressing AI as long semis versus short something else have made defensives like Hershey move inversely to SMH.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Staples strength may be a mechanical pair-trade artifact, not fundamental.
insights.quote: if you want to know what Hershey's is doing this year, just tell me what SMH is doing

themes.theme: AI fundamentals still intact: compute is tight

insights.claim: GPU availability from neoclouds, tracked since 2023, collapsed with this year's agentic explosion; B200 availability is at zero and rental prices have crept higher.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Compute demand still exceeds supply; no sign of overbuild.

insights.claim: Standard data center models, including 314 Research's, assumed roughly 25% annual declines in GPU rents; instead rents are rising, which is not in anyone's cash-flow model.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Data center economics may be materially better than consensus models assume.
insights.quote: our core assumption was a 25%annual decline in rents. And so we haven't seen that.

insights.claim: Longer-dated GPU rental prices are now in contango; Pies argues this is a capacity premium from buyers locking in capacity, a bullish sign, not the bearish signal contango implies in oil.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Don't import oil-market heuristics to compute futures curves.
insights.quote: You have a capacity premium that's emerging here.

insights.claim: Anthropic's S1 shows revenue per dollar of compute spend rising from 57 cents in Q2 of last year to $2.08, with a slight Q3 dip, while revenue per inference-compute dollar rose every quarter including Q3.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Lab unit economics are improving, undermining the AI ROI bear case.
insights.quote: revenue per dollar of compute spend has trended gone from 57 cents in Q2 of last year up to $2.08.

insights.claim: Hyperscaler cloud revenues began ramping in Q2 reporting, and Pies believes the AI return-on-investment debate is being ground down to nothing.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Returns on AI capex are becoming visible in reported numbers.

insights.claim: 314 Research's satellite pacing model of every data center under construction (groundbreaking to energized shell) shows no supply shortfall versus semiconductor revenue estimates, and projects 27+ GW additional coming online over 2027.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Supply pacing supports top-line semis estimates for 2027.
insights.quote: there's going to be an additional 27 plus gigawatts coming online over 2027

insights.claim: Hyperscalers and semis selling off together is inconsistent with a supply-crunch story, since a crunch would raise compute prices and lower capex needs, making hyperscalers more attractive; Pies reads it as a liquidation/VaR shock.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Joint selling looks technical, creating a hyperscaler buying opportunity once risk stabilizes.
insights.quote: I already want to own the hyperscalers when this thing's said and done

insights.claim: Pies' fundamental conviction would change only if GPU availability spiked and rental prices plummeted, signalling overbuild; he sees no signs of that and expects any supply shock to produce underbuild.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: GPU rental/availability are the kill switch to watch for the AI bull case.

themes.theme: Macro risk: the Fed pivots its focus to the AI build-out

insights.claim: Before the Iran war SOFR futures priced about 75 bp more cuts; pricing swung to as many as six hikes through 2027 as the Fed moved from a cut cycle to a realized hike cycle.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: The rates regime has flipped from supportive to restrictive.

insights.claim: The 10-year Treasury's correlation has shifted from oil to the Nasdaq, signalling the Fed's inflation focus has handed off from the war/oil to the AI build-out, while SOFR-10-year correlation stayed above 90%.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: The Fed may keep hiking until something breaks in AI funding markets; there's no clean exit via an oil ceasefire.
insights.quote: the risk is that the Fed doesn't stop until they've broken something in the AI trade in the funding markets.

insights.claim: The Fed cut from 2024 through last year into a ramping capex cycle, something never seen before, making late-cycle inflation pressure unsurprising.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Easing into a capex boom may have seeded today's inflation and hikes.
insights.quote: we've never seen the Fed cutting into a CAPEX cycle.

insights.claim: Pies has reversed his earlier view that the Fed cannot dent the AI build-out: once capex shifted from free cash flow to external debt and equity funding, rate hikes became a real limiting factor, especially for semis.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Rate sensitivity of AI capex has risen; semis are most exposed.

insights.claim: 314 Research estimates VC-backed startups are about 25% of AI lab ARR, so a 2022-style VC funding freeze from hikes could remove a large chunk of lab revenue.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: VC funding conditions are a hidden transmission channel to AI lab revenue.
insights.quote: VC startup companies are about 25%of lab ARR.

insights.claim: Pies thinks the Fed ultimately won't kill the AI trade: Warsh has already wobbled on financial conditions, another credit wobble would end hikes, and damaging the AI trade carries more political heat than inflation.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: An implicit 'Fed put' on AI credit stress limits tail risk.

insights.claim: With the 2-year around 4.6%, Pies expects one more Fed hike then a hawkish hold; dropping the hawkish bias would let the 2-year fall and the curve flatten, re-accelerating sectors crowded out by AI, so he sees chop rather than recession.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Base case is choppy growth, not recession; rate-sensitive sectors are the release valve.
insights.quote: I think the Fed has one more hike in it and basically that that they're done.

insights.claim: Pies believes the next big oil move depends on Iran geopolitics with a wider range of outcomes than consensus, which crowded into expecting renewed bombing; the US blockade is working (Iranian floating storage down) but needs patience.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Don't assume escalation; a deal is a real path for oil.

insights.claim: Pies expects a deal with Iran is more likely post-election than pre-election, and says the situation must be resolved in roughly 45 days as SPR, European and G7 releases run down, with China pressuring Iran.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: A near-term catalyst window for oil exists over the next ~45 days.
insights.quote: this thing's going to need to get figured out over the I call it the next 45 days

insights.claim: Over 60% of global VLCCs were laden, crack spreads and middle distillates are blown out, diesel has been above $200 per barrel for months, and Singapore gasoil cracks were above $70.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Physical oil markets are deeply dislocated; distillate inflation persists.

insights.claim: Oil futures positioning is squared with no extremes to fade, so Pies recommends an energy overweight within a balanced portfolio as the only hedge against the war going sideways.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Hold energy as portfolio insurance.
insights.quote: you have to have an overweight energy within a balanced portfolio because it's just there's no other way to hedge the risk

insights.claim: Elevated crack spreads normally resolve through refiners retooling toward middle distillates plus demand destruction; absent a structural oddity like the old crude export ban they are temporary, and refiners bidding for crude will keep oil sticky-high.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Don't get married to refiners; expect crack compression but firm crude.
insights.quote: the refining business is not a business to get married to.

insights.claim: Pies argues the Iran war was a strategic miscalculation that exposed overstretched US capabilities, accelerating a multipolar world, reduced US presence in the Gulf, and possibly the energy transition.
insights.speaker: Warren Pies
insights.so_what: Structural geopolitical shift supports higher risk premia and energy-security themes.
